acv.quote: Two hundred and ten K ACV.

data.reason: Won membership billing only, front desks stay with Global. Greg, the controller, signed after seeing which of their own failed renewals could be recovered, not just Maya's choice, as the rep first said.

trigger.action: Lead with failed cards hiding inside the churn numbers boards see.
trigger.why: Board-reported churn rose two quarters, and splitting it showed failed cards were a bigger share than expected.
trigger.quote: The second bucket was a lot bigger than anyone expected.

decider.action: Show the controller recovered revenue in their own renewal data, not averages.
decider.why: Greg, the controller, sat on the contract two weeks, then signed four days after seeing their own failed renewals.
decider.quote: Maya chose us. Greg decided whether anybody got chosen.

competitor.action: Say plainly what leaving the current processor costs, including contract exit fees.
competitor.why: After Global Payments' offer, as Maya relayed it, questions turned to contract terms and Greg asked about termination fees twice.
competitor.quote: Greg asked about termination fees twice.

message.action: Cut the global growth headline for a mostly US customer.
message.why: The rep opened with the global slide for a business with US studios and a few in Canada, and got silence.
message.quote: Silence. I opened with the global slide.

proof.action: Add proof our reader works inside studio software on one screen.
proof.why: Maya asked to see check-in and a sale on one screen, we couldn't show it live, and front desks stayed with Global.

words.action: Say 'members who never meant to leave' instead of failed payment recovery.
words.why: Maya's own phrase from earlier in the call. The wording question itself was put off to Slack.
words.quote: members who never meant to leave.
